meta.expect: After Hale owns the procedural mistake she gives a small sign of ground (a flat 'Okay', uses Hale's name, writes it down) but does not give up her position on the essay.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. My school's procedure says I should have called first. I was wrong, and I've asked the office to note that.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now, on what basis was the zero given, and what else do you have besides a machine's score?
I still have a real concern about the essay itself, and I'd like to show you why.
A concern isn't evidence, Hale. Show me, and it had better have dates on it.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in the play. Here is the scene; you can read it.
Turn the screen, I'll read it myself. Misquoting Shakespeare doesn't make a seventeen-year-old a cheat, Hale. Did anyone ask Owen where that line came from before the zero went in?
